instruction: Write a short summary of the passage below.
context: Institute of Coastal Science researchers ran a study of sleep quality over 16 months with 13720 volunteers. Lead author Arun Prakash noted the design was observational, so causation remains unproven. The dataset will be made available to other researchers on request. Funding came from a mix of institutional grants and a regional foundation. The group found the primary measure up 15 percent, with the strongest results among participants recruited in Gdansk. The protocol was registered before data collection began. Two graduate students presented preliminary findings at a conference last year.
response: Arun Prakash and colleagues at Institute of Coastal Science followed 13720 people for 16 months and saw sleep quality improve 15 percent, with the largest effect in Gdansk; the study is observational, not causal.

instruction: Provide a brief summary of this report.
context: Institute of Coastal Science staff followed 5080 participants over 57 months in a study of commuting stress. An advisory panel met twice during the study to review safety reports. The protocol was registered before data collection began. Oscar Delgado, who led the work, cautioned that the study was observational and cannot establish cause. A replication attempt by an unrelated group is reportedly in the planning stage. Recruitment relied largely on notices posted in community centres and clinics. response: Oscar Delgado and colleagues at Institute of Coastal Science followed 5080 people for 57 months and saw commuting stress improve 28 percent, with the largest effect in Fukuoka; the study is observational, not causal.
